item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
item.description:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia

Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.

Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Mural of Macklemore wrapped in Palestinian flag painted on Gaza ruins
item.description:
Mural of Macklemore wrapped in Palestinian flag painted on Gaza ruins

Artists in Gaza have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour for calling for a "Free Palestine".

The mural, on a slab that leans against ruined buildings surrounded by rubble, depicts the "Thrift Shop" rapper raising a fist in the air.

"Thank you for using your voice for Palestine," it reads.

"We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way," said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai al-Helo.

"As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under," she told Reuters. "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings."

Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran's musical lineup over remarks on stage criticizing Israel's military assault in Gaza.

Report by Reuters

item.description:
Macron to convene G7 over energy crisis, says France working to reopen Hormuz

French President Emmanuel Macron has said that he would convene a G7 meeting in the coming weeks to coordinate responses to the energy crisis caused by the Iran war, while reiterating France was working to facilitate the peaceful reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

Macron said the meeting would focus on coordinating strategic stockpile levels, cooperation on exports and production capacity, and possible releases of strategic reserves.

Macron said that the aim of the meeting was to strengthen cooperation and avoid unnecessary tensions between G7 countries and their key partners.

He said France had initiated an international defence mission with the International Maritime Organization last April aimed at escorting tankers and container ships through the strategic waterway once an agreement was reached.

Macron said reopening Hormuz depended on a deal between Iran and the United States, which he said appeared unlikely in the short term.

The comments came as France faces growing pressure over sharply higher fuel prices, with Macron acknowledging that pump prices had reached historic levels and were putting pressure on the purchasing power of households.

Report by AFP

item.description:
Former Palestinian minister to reveal message Sinwar wanted Israel to hear

Former Palestinian Authority minister, Sufian Abu Zaida, has said he acted as a go-between for Israel and Hamas before 7 October 2023, and has promised to disclose the message Yahya Sinwar asked him to pass on.

“Over the next few days, I will discuss the nature of the contacts I held over a year and a half between Israel and Hamas, which were aimed at reaching a deal to secure the release of the prisoners held by Hamas,” Abu Zaida said in a video statement on Friday.

He was referring to two Israeli civilians who were being held by Hamas for years before the 7 October 2023 invasion, along with the bodies of two IDF soldiers.

“I will also discuss the message that… Sinwar asked me to convey to the Israeli side,” Abu Zaida said, adding that he would be revealing the details in an interview with the Egyptian Al-Ghad TV channel in the coming days.

Hours later, Israeli journalist Shlomi Eldar identified him as "Coal Eyes", the unnamed Fatah interlocutor in his Haaretz report earlier this month, which created a furore in Israel. 

The report alleged that Sinwar, frustrated by stalled talks, warned Israel of a "zilzal", Arabic for earthquake. Haaretz report said the warning had reached Emirati president Mohammed bin Zayed, who then phoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Netanyahu has denies that any such call took place.

item.description:

Yemen’s foreign minister, Afrah Alzouba, has said that Yemen is not “an Iranian bargaining chip” and that its future is “determined by Yemenis through their state and national path”.

In a discussion with Russian news agency, Sputnik, Alzouba emphasized that restoring the state is a “pillar for regional security and the protection of international navigation”, according to statement posted on X by the country’s foreign ministry. 

The post said that during the discussion, Alzouba addressed the escalation by “the terrorist Houthi militia” in the western coast and Bab al-Mandab, its humanitarian repercussions, its implications for national and regional security, and international trade routes, as well as relations with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Saudi commander says security of international waterways collective responsibility
item.description:
Saudi commander says security of international waterways collective responsibility

Rear Admiral Abdullah bin Salem al-Shehri, commander of the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition (MMDC), has said that protection of international waterways is an international responsibility, and warned that “any threat to international maritime security will be deterred”.

Al Shehri was addressing the press after the coalition’s fourth planning meeting concluded in Jeddah on Friday.
 
The MMDC is a 14-country military alliance formed in July to ensure global waterways around the Arabian Peninsula, including the Gulf of Aden, the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and the Red Sea, remain open to international traffic.

The meeting in Jeddah was part of the coalition’s "ongoing transition from the founding stage to the actual operational stage, having reached Initial operational capability," the ministry said in a statement on X.

The meeting was attended by representatives of "41 brotherly and friendly countries," and EU representatives also took part.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Report: Australia's reluctance to join settlement sanctions disappoints EU diplomats
item.description:
Report: Australia's reluctance to join settlement sanctions disappoints EU diplomats

European diplomats have expressed surprise and disappointment after Australia declined to join a UK-led move to target trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, according to an ABC report based on interviews with diplomatic sources in several countries.

Twelve other nations had backed the UK’s decision, saying they would commit to, or consider, action on trade with illegal settlements. Canada was the only signatory from outside Europe.

Four diplomatic sources told the ABC that Australia took part in the discussions until close to the statement's finalisation and signalled openness to further action. It then decided not to sign.

"Some sources speculated the pressure Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has been under since the Bondi terror attacks, and the criticism from Jewish groups that the federal government has not been strong enough on antisemitism, may have played a part in Australia's decision not to announce sanctions last week," according to the report.

"Other sources suggested internal politics meant the federal government could not pull together an aligned position in time to join the statement."

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Morning recap
item.description:
Morning recap

Good morning Middle East Eye readers,
If you're just joining us, here are key developments from across the region:

•    US President Donald Trump has signed into law legislation extending existing US sanctions on Iran to 2031 and expanding sanctions, tariffs and other restrictions on Russia.

•    Explosions were heard in Riyadh on Saturday, AFP reported, while Saudi civil defence authorities issued, and later withdrew, alerts for several provinces.

•    Yemen’s Human Rights Ministry accused the Houthis of attacking and looting Saudi-funded humanitarian and medical facilities in al-Khawkhah and other areas along the western coast of the country.

•    Yemen's Houthis said that Saudi Arabia had launched 26 strikes against areas under their control in the past 24 hours, amid continuing fighting between the Iran-aligned movement and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government.

•    Turkey has revoked the operating licence of Iran’s Bank Mellat, which remains on the US Treasury’s sanctions list, as Washington intensifies economic pressure on Tehran.

•    Saudi Arabia has informed at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will not receive crude oil allocations in October, as the war in the Middle East hits global energy markets. 

•    Former Palestinian Authority minister, Sufian Abu Zaida, has said he acted as a go-between for Israel and Hamas before 7 October 2023, and has promised to disclose the message Yahya Sinwar asked him to pass on.

•    Three Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip, Al Jazeera reported, citing local hospital sources.

•    Yemen’s foreign minister, Afrah Alzouba, has said that Yemen is not “an Iranian bargaining chip” and that its future is “determined by Yemenis through their state and national path”.

•    Rear Admiral Abdullah bin Salem al-Shehri, commander of the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition (MMDC), has said that protection of international waterways is an international responsibility, and warned that “any threat to international maritime security will be deterred”.

•    US Central Command (Centcom) said it has redirected 105 commercial vessels since the US enforced a naval blockade against Iran.
